title: Check yourself: what a subclass inherits

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A superclass has a `private void log()` method, and its subclass declares its own `void log()`. What does the page say the subclass's `log()` is?

options.text: An override, which runs whenever the superclass itself calls log()
options.says: The page says private methods cannot be overridden, so the superclass's own calls still reach its private method.

options.text: A separate new method, because the private one is not inherited
options.says: The page says private methods are not inherited, so a same-named method in the subclass is a new method, not an override.

options.text: A compile error, because that name is already taken in the superclass
options.says: The page says you can define such a method; it compiles as a new method.

questions.stem: A subclass sits in a different package from its superclass. Which of the superclass's members does the page say it does not inherit?

options.text: Those marked protected, and those marked private
options.says: The page says protected members are inherited and accessible in subclasses, in any package.

options.text: Those marked public, and those marked protected
options.says: The page says public and protected members are both inherited.

options.text: Those with no access modifier, and those marked private
options.says: The page says default members are inherited only in the same package, and private members never are.

concepts: Public and protected members are inherited, package-private ones only within the package, and private ones never.
A private method is not inherited, so a same-named subclass method is a new method, not an override.
